25.original: Inspect the Ondo Cups from the survey point.

26.original: Use the mythril knife to collect scrapings from the remnant wall.

28.original: Find a structure which resembles those in the copy of the Qitana Ravel mural, then inspect it from the survey point.

48.original: ...Ah, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. Have you learned aught of note?

49.original: Fascinating...and precisely the sort of information I was hoping to hear.

50.original: In fact, if you have a moment, I'd like to borrow your eyes to confirm a theory I've been working on. Come.

51.original: Now, there are two tasks I would have you perform.

52.original: The first requires you to inspect the buildings which surround the Ondo settlement, and note their most distinctive characteristics.

53.original: For the second, I wish you to use this knife to take scrapings from one of the remnant walls.

54.original: Pray be as thorough as you can. I shall be waiting here for the results of your investigations.

55.original: 'Tis strange to be here, under the ocean. It seems a lifetime ago that we stood amidst the trees of Rak'tika...

56.original: Inspect the structures of the Ondo Cups for distinctive features. You may move the camera, as well as zoom in and out. Target a building and examine it with <hex:020825E4E95101FF10024804F2022203EE81910248020103FF0E021E021003202F20021E02090303>.

57.original: You set the point of the knife against the wall, but even after applying considerable pressure, you cannot remove so much as a flake of stone.

59.original: Yes, I would agree that the windows are most distinctive. 'Twould seem the structures appear the same to both your sight and mine...

60.original: And you say you could not so much as scratch the wall? Even with all your might behind the blade?

61.original: <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>, everywhere I turn in this place, my gaze is drawn by peculiar materials for which I do not have a name.

62.original: The buildings I had you investigate are prime examples. They may appear to be constructed of ordinary stone, but I assure you it is nothing of the sort...

63.original: If pressed, I would describe the substance as a composite of several mineral properties, blended to create a material of unparalleled durability.

64.original: Even the Ronkan Empire, once the greatest power in Norvrandt, produced nothing which compares to this level of perfection.

65.original: But if not the Ronkans, then who? Who were these ancients the Ondo claim as the architects of their sanctuary?

66.original: I suspect our answer lies with the reason Emet-Selch withdrew here to the Tempest.

67.original: He may simply have wished to retreat somewhere mere mortals would struggle to reach...but there are many such remote locations. Why here, specifically?

68.original: Emet-Selch is devoted to his role, and thus we might assume his choice of stronghold somehow serves the Ascian agenda.

69.original: Or mayhap...'tis a place more dear to him than any other.

71.original: Are you saying this was built by ancient Ascians...?

72.original: Could this place provide power to Emet-Selch?

74.original: That is my theory, that these structures are remnants of a time before history─of a star that was yet whole and unbroken.

75.original: That was my first thought as well. Yet no matter how superior the materials, a ruin is just a ruin. 'Tis naught that would decide a battle's outcome.

76.original: Which brings us to my second theory: that he has some other, more personal connection to this site. What if these structures are remnants of a time before history─of a star that was yet whole and unbroken?

77.original: It is my theory that these structures are remnants of a time before history─of a star that was yet whole and unbroken.

78.original: Such traces in the Source would have been obliterated by the succession of Umbral Calamities, but here in the First they might have remained untouched for millennia...

79.original: ...A copy of the mural in the Qitana Ravel. Almet presented it to me during my visit to Fanow, after our victory in Kholusia.

80.original: Here, in the first scene...<hex:02100103>By Emet-Selch's own words, it depicts a city of eons past and the disaster which befell it.

81.original: The design is much simplified, of course, but do you see the similarities between its towers and those you have just inspected?

82.original: We are close to the truth, I feel. Let us search the surrounds for another tower─one which matches the picture near enough to remove all doubt.

83.original: From what I have seen, naught more than sand and more sand lies to the east, and the south held no such structures. I suggest we try our luck further to the northwest.

84.original: You may view the Qitana Ravel mural at any time during this quest by using the relevant item in the <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>Key Items<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> menu.

85.original: The quest destination will not be displayed on the map. You must search for a structure which resembles the buildings in the mural, then inspect it from the survey point. The survey point will be found nearby, in a location which allows a full view of the structure.

86.original: Search for a structure which resembles one of the buildings in this mural, then inspect it from the survey point. The survey point will be found nearby, in a location which allows a full view of the structure.

87.original: According to Y'shtola's investigations, the area further northwest of the Ondo Cups may be a good place to start.

88.original: Aye... This is the mural writ large...

89.original: Though I cannot guess at its purpose, it must have been an imposing sight. How much of the tower's height lies hidden beneath the ground, I wonder...

90.original: Centuries of our history have settled upon such ruins. Countless layers of dust and sediment...

91.original: ...An entire civilization, its existence forgotten by all except a handful of Ascians.

92.original: And yet it did exist. They lived here, in this city...

93.original: But let us focus on what we've learned thus far. The Ondo chieftain spoke of mysteries stirring─of a land illuminated.

94.original: Judging by his words, he believes this phenomenon related to the ancients' return.

95.original: Thus can we surmise that what the Ondo saw shining in the abyss was, in all likelihood, yet another remnant of this age-old civilization.

96.original: And who else would “light the lanterns” as Ryne put it, than Emet-Selch himself? 'Tis almost certain he is there!

97.original: But if we are to find this stronghold in a timely manner, it seems gaining the Ondo's trust remains our swiftest path forward.

98.original: I only hope our deeds are enough to win them over...
